headline: 556/1000 bez zmian we wtorek rano: noc nie przyniosła nowych zdarzeń kredytowych; dziś inflacja w USA i wyniki CoreWeave.
headline_en: 556/1000, unchanged on Tuesday morning: the night brought no new credit events; US inflation and CoreWeave's results are due today.
summary: Wynik 556/1000 – bez zmian od wczorajszego wieczornego raportu. Nocny przegląd wiadomości nie przyniósł nowych zdarzeń kredytowych, obniżek ratingów ani stanowych wstrzymań budowy centrów danych. Giełdy w Azji odbiły (Nikkei prawie +3% na spółkach AI), co nie zmienia odczytów. Dziś po południu inflacja CPI w USA, od której zależy wycena grudniowej podwyżki stóp Fed, a wieczorem wyniki CoreWeave – najbardziej zadłużonego wynajmującego moc obliczeniową AI.
summary_en: The score is 556/1000 – unchanged since yesterday evening's report. The overnight news sweep brought no new credit events, rating downgrades or state pauses on data-center construction. Asian stock markets rebounded (the Nikkei up almost 3% on AI stocks), which does not change the readings. This afternoon brings US CPI inflation, on which the pricing of a December Fed rate hike depends, and in the evening the results of CoreWeave – the most indebted renter of AI computing power.

New 29 Oct: AWS +39% y/y in Q3 (USD 46.0bn, fastest in nearly 5 years; Amazon release – primary source); Amazon booked USD 9.5bn of gains on its Anthropic investment in Q3 2025 (conflict of interest). signals.note_en: New 9 Nov – lasting-event check: Ohio (the Tax Credit Authority has not resumed considering requests) and Illinois (DCEO has not resumed Data Center Investment Program agreements; Senate session 17–19 Nov) – end conditions not met. The US Senate returns on 9 Nov; the bipartisan permitting bill (Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act) is slated as its first vote – it speeds permits and adds energy-use reporting, it does not restrict build-out. 🔴 unchanged. New 7 Nov evening (note): CBS News (6 Nov) – on 3 Nov voters passed at least 44 of 47 local proposals restricting data centers (from bans to temporary moratoria), with a few results still pending; these are local measures (🟡 level), the 🔴 status rests on the state tax-incentive pauses in Ohio and Illinois. New 7 Nov – correcting an oversight, second 🔴 event: on 5 Jun Illinois Governor Pritzker directed DCEO to stop entering new agreements under the state Data Center Investment Program tax incentive from 1 Jul 2026 (governor's release; Fortune, Bloomberg Law, Insurance Journal – primary and independent secondary); agreements made before 1 Jul are honoured. Brownstein tracker (updated 22 Sep): incentive "paused for new applicants as of July 2026"; no reports of it being restored. Suspension of a state tax break → 🔴, registered as a lasting event; alongside Ohio → stacked_events = 1. Illinois Senate session 17–19 Nov and 1–3 Dec (possible data-center legislation); House Speaker Welch said the pause lacked the Democratic caucus's support. New signal (since 6 Nov). On 27 May Ohio Governor DeWine paused the Ohio Tax Credit Authority's consideration of new data-center tax exemption requests while the legislature studies the issue (governor's release; WOSU, Spectrum News – primary and independent secondary); according to Luminix the pause runs until January 2027. Suspension of a state tax break → 🔴, registered as a lasting event. Background (note): opponents of the build-out won 40 of 41 local votes on 3 Nov (Ballotpedia via Luminix), Democrats take Congress, PUCT rules on transmission cost allocation for large loads (law SB 6) due by 31 Dec; Texas's SB 6 as a separate 🔴 event needs its effective date checked – not counted in stacked_events. The permit pauses in Texas and New York count in F1.

Aurora (Kolorado): rada miasta 26.10 ma głosować nad bezterminowym moratorium burmistrza Mike'a Coffmana, przełożonym z 19.10 (Colorado Politics, Denver Gazette – źródła wtórne); wcześniej odrzucono 6-miesięczne moratorium na rzecz przepisów lokalizacyjnych. q75 bez zmian. 26.10 (Telecom Reseller za raportem S&P Global Ratings – źródło wtórne): S&P potwierdza, że wpływ sprzeciwu lokalnego na ocenianie przez nią transakcje jest na razie ograniczony. signals.note_en: New 9 Nov – lasting-event check: Texas (TCEQ has not resumed permits; ERCOT audit report around 10 Dec), New York (Executive Order 62 in force; DPS conference and report by 31 Dec), Oregon (DEQ order to 1 Jul 2027) – end conditions not met. Review found no new state moratoria in force and no cancelled signed projects; Colorado Springs rejected Project Taurus (Denver Gazette, 8 Nov) – a local decision. q150 unchanged. New 7 Nov evening (note, no status change): Crusoe confirmed on 6 Nov the sale to Google of its unfinished campus project in Laramie County (Wyoming; with Tallgrass, up to 10 GW eventually) – according to Bloomberg (6 Nov) Crusoe found no tenant for it, and Google had raised concerns about costs and timing; a day earlier Google announced a USD 17bn investment in the campus (Bloomberg, The Next Web – secondary). The project changes owner and is not cancelled – q150 unchanged. New 7 Nov (note): sweep found no new state moratoria in force and no cancellations of signed projects; on 6 Nov President Trump wrote that he would work with states that want to benefit from AI (Newsweek) – no legal action. q150 unchanged. New 6 Nov late morning – q75 → q150 (correcting an oversight): state-level pauses that stop new data-center projects are in force in two states. Texas: on 21 Sep Governor Abbott ordered TCEQ to halt all environmental permits (air, water, stormwater) for data centers until ERCOT completes its audit, including facilities with their own power (Houston Public Media; law firms Troutman, Bracewell, Foley, Baker Donelson – primary and independent sources); audit report around 10 Dec, no date for permits to resume. Texas is about 27% of planned US GW (Wells Fargo). New York: Governor Hochul's Executive Order 62 of 14 Jul pauses DEC discretionary environmental permits for projects ≥ 50 MW for up to a year (Hodgson Russ, Davis Polk, Phillips Lytle). Oregon: Governor Kotek's directive of 9 Oct halting new DEQ permits until 1 Jul 2027 (earlier note). The q150 condition (moratoria in force in 2+ states covering ≥ 10% of planned capacity) is met; earlier reports wrongly treated state moratoria as not yet in force – the Texas pause has run since 21 Sep. Events registered as lasting; stacked_events = 0 because q150 already covers both states. Pledges by the new governors of Texas, Georgia and Ohio count in B5, not here. Counter-argument: the pauses are temporary (until the audit, up to a year), and construction with permits already issued continues. New 6 Nov morning (note, no status change): sweep found no new project cancellations or moratoria in force; Reuters (5 Nov) – UBS estimates about 30% of expected US data-center capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from possible construction pauses; IREN is delaying deliveries to Microsoft (MarketScreener). q75 – near q100. New 5 Nov evening (no status change, near q100): Bloomberg (via Reuters, TradingView) – Microsoft is tightening oversight of some Nebius, IREN and Nscale projects, will not exercise an option to more than double its Nscale agreement in Texas, and earlier pulled out as anchor tenant at Loughton (Essex) where grid-connection delays stretch into the 2030s; IREN – cabling problems at its Texas campus may push completion back by weeks or months (Microsoft spokesperson). UBS estimates that possible construction pauses put about 30% of expected US data-center capacity additions in 2028 at risk (Reuters). q75 kept: the delays concern individual projects and are measured in weeks to months, and a declined option is not the cancellation of a signed agreement; moratoria are not yet in effect. q100 would require formal cancellations of signed projects or bans in effect. New 5 Nov morning (note, no status change): during the campaign Gina Hinojosa said that as governor she would issue a moratorium on new data centers and their approvals until laws are passed and call a special legislative session (campaign site, Fox 4 – secondary); she takes office in January 2027, so no moratorium is in effect. Wells Fargo: Texas holds about 27% of planned US data-center gigawatts (24/7 Wall St.). q75 – near q100. New 4 Nov evening: results of the 3 Nov votes (Fortune 4 Nov; Yahoo News, StockAnalysis, TheGridSight – independent secondary sources, unofficial results): of 41 local votes in 10 states, 21 took place in 18 Ohio municipalities; at least 14 municipalities passed bans or restrictions (including Sunbury – a ban on centers ≥ 25 MW, Pataskala, Trenton about 80% for a ban, Urbana, Defiance, Piqua, Granville); in Wilmington about 80% rejected rezoning; in Ashville voters backed scrapping the village agreement with EdgeConneX for a campus already under construction (the referendum does not directly stop construction – legal effect unclear). In Texas (about 27% of planned US data-center GW per Wells Fargo) Gina Hinojosa (Democrat), who campaigned for tougher construction limits, was elected governor (CNBC 4 Nov); Democrats take Congress, which analysts link to hearings rather than quick legislation (Reuters via Yahoo Finance). Many restrictions are not yet in effect and no project has been formally cancelled → q75 unchanged, near q100 (condition partly met). New 4 Nov (note): results of the 3 Nov local data-center ballot measures (incl. 18–21 Ohio communities, e.g. Urbana, Trenton) not yet confirmed; the statewide Ohio amendment banning large data centers did not make the ballot. q75 unchanged. On 29 Sep FERC only partly approved PJM's emergency procurement (6.8 GW shortfall for 2028/29), the auction is suspended. A wave of local moratoria in October: Raleigh, Oakland, San Francisco (6 Oct), Brighton CO, Dover DE (18 months, 12 Oct), Shelby County TN (first reading). New: Milwaukee's Common Council on 13 Oct unanimously (13–0) adopted a one-year ban on building and expanding data centers (Urban Milwaukee); Oregon Governor Tina Kotek, in a letter dated 9 Oct (made public 13 Oct), told the state environmental agency DEQ to pause new water and air permits for data centers until 1 Jul 2027 – in effect the first state-level pause in a major hub (Oregon Capital Chronicle, OPB, DCD); it may affect Amazon's planned campus in Boardman. Also Forest Grove OR (120 days) and Elizabeth City NC (18 months). New on 14 Oct (Boston Globe, a single source): the Westfield (Massachusetts) planning board unanimously refused to extend a 2021 permit for Servistar's USD 4bn (274 MW) campus. The Shelby County/Memphis moratorium vote was postponed to 20 Oct (WREG). No other new project cancellations and no new PJM news; construction with permits already issued continues – q75, near q100. New 19–20 Oct (Seoul Economic Daily on 19 Oct citing the FT and the firm Reglayer – a single secondary source): at least 47 large US data-center projects delayed, withdrawn or blocked this year (a "conservative" estimate); Bernstein: about 35% of planned US projects likely to be built. Reports of Microsoft pulling out of a lease with Nscale in Loughton (UK) unconfirmed – available sources describe a grid-connection delay to 2027. Status q75 unchanged, near q100. Result on 20 Oct (WSMV, Fox13, CNN – independent secondary sources): the Memphis City Council rejected an 18-month moratorium on a 6–6 tie but adopted (7–5) Ordinance 18 – a 135-day moratorium together with rules on siting, construction and expansion of data centers; Mayor Paul Young ordered a 90-day study on regulating large data centers. The shorter pause does not change the assessment – q75, near q100. New 23 Oct (Bloomberg – single secondary source): in a report S&P Global Ratings warns that moratoriums and cancellations driven by local opposition may lead to rating downgrades of data-center projects – a warning, not a rating action; q75 unchanged. Aurora (Colorado): on 26 Oct the city council is due to vote on Mayor Mike Coffman's indefinite moratorium, postponed from 19 Oct (Colorado Politics, Denver Gazette – secondary sources); a six-month moratorium was rejected earlier in favour of siting rules. q75 unchanged. 26 Oct (Telecom Reseller citing the S&P Global Ratings report – secondary source): S&P says the impact of local opposition on the transactions it rates is so far limited. The Aurora vote result is expected overnight (Polish time). q75 unchanged. Result on 26 Oct (Denver Gazette, 9NEWS – two independent secondary sources): the Aurora council did not adopt the indefinite moratorium – 6 votes for and 5 against, short of the required two-thirds majority; projects already filed would have proceeded anyway. q75 unchanged, near q100.
